Landed less the Quipu round-trip. datalinks/ parses alphax.txt deterministically (no model: it is fixed-arity CSV with inline column docs, and a hallucinated tech prerequisite tagged canonical is the worst failure available to us), emits the smac: graph with all three anti-masquerade predicates on every node, and serves a static briefing plus action-space-scoped grounding through the Retriever seam. Verified against a real 1281-line alphax.txt: 88 techs, 133 facilities (50 Disabled), 64 SP rows, 2579 triples round-tripping through rdflib. Three bugs found by checking rather than eyeballing: (1) two facilities have commas inside effect text, so SP detection had to move from row arity to 'last five fields are ints'; (2) Turtle PN_LOCAL forbids '/', so smac:tech/biogen was a parse error that looked perfectly reasonable -- fixed with per-class prefixes and rdflib is now a dev dep gating it; (3) Disable in a preq column means excluded-from-game, not a prerequisite, and treating it as a tech would have invented 50 fake edges. Also: alphax.txt's own header calls the facility column 'Free' (grants the facility free at new bases), not obsoletedBy as knowledge-architecture.md says -- the file wins, noted in rdf.py. Added NA_EXTRACTION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5) as a separate cheaper dial from the brain's, for K3's postgame episode extraction which IS genuine model work. Remaining: load the graph into a running Quipu and serve retrieval from it rather than the parsed structs -- folded into na-6ce (K2). 21 tests against a synthetic excerpt; the real alphax.txt is game data and is never committed.

Split: the budgeting half landed, the semantic half is blocked and now has its own bead. Landed: datalinks/budget.py enforces an approximate token ceiling and sheds tactics before rules -- rules are correctness, tactics are optimization, and that ordering is the same precedence the prompt enforces, so the budget cannot invert the trust ordering to save tokens. A single greedy pass in list order would have let a long tactic at the front crowd out a rule behind it, so it fills by precedence class instead, and it keeps scanning past an oversized fact since a later shorter one may still fit. Nothing is dropped silently: the surviving grounding carries an explicit '[N tactics omitted for token budget]' line, because a truncated prompt that reads as complete is the same failure shape as the all-fallback run. Wired as QuipuRetriever(token_budget=N), default 0 = unbounded since the action-space cap already bounds the common case. BLOCKED (na-9tk): quipu_context and quipu_hybrid_search need vectors; quipu knot does not embed, --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', --features onnx gives the runtime not a model, and huggingface.co is not on the cloud Trusted allowlist so the model cannot be fetched from a session. Approach refuted and reverted; the cost problem re-filed as na-vbe with the shape a fix must have. Option 1 (rank then truncate) was implemented and measured over 20 decisions per config on Haiku: utilisation 0.22 to 0.28, but only because the denominator shrank, and the decision changed (Network Node 19/20 to Research Hospital 15/20) with stability falling 0.95 to 0.75. The ranking rule predicts citation worse than chance - 0.43 of citations in its top four against 0.50 for noise - and the one fact cited in 20 of 20 decisions ranked fifth of eight. Generalisable finding recorded in docs/quipu-integration.md: grounding is one fact per option, so top-k truncation removes the explanation of an option rather than removing information, and an unexplained option loses; any such truncation biases the choice whatever it ranks by. Shipped from this work: DatalinksRetriever now emits fact_ids, without which the K1 path could not be cited against at all and utilisation was structurally unmeasurable. Harness kept at scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py.

The adapter emits subjects itself now: na_observe_base_hurry writes subjects:[prod_name(item)] alongside the existing item key (scbrown/thinker src/neural.cpp). Until now the only thing setting it was the bridge in scripts/decision_stability.py, so the real contract path had the gap and only the measurement rig worked around it.

The bridge now prefers an adapter-supplied subjects and keeps the item fallback for observations recorded before this landed - a stored run is evidence, and re-scoring it should not require the adapter version that produced it.

Also documented in docs/contract.md, since the field had no entry at all: subjects is what makes a surface groundable when its options are not entities, and naming a subject cannot bias the choice the way grounding one option would, because every option on such a surface concerns the same entity.

Not yet re-measured: the 0.60 stability figure that motivates this was taken with no grounding at all, and whether grounding the subject moves it needs a live run or an eval. Worth an arm in evals/ once base.hurry has a world view worth pinning.

Both fields now stamped on all four observations (scbrown/thinker src/neural.cpp). surface_id was already there; trace and fairness were not.

traceparent makes the adapter the trace root because the game is the root of the causality. The ids are derived rather than random deliberately: the engine's RNG is the game's RNG, so drawing from it would perturb a seeded game just by observing it. Turn, faction, base and the per-turn call sequence already identify a decision uniquely within a run, plus a wall-clock session salt to separate two runs of the same save.

fairness stamps only what the engine knows - is_human(faction) and *DiffLevel - with an explicitly EMPTY handicaps list, and the orchestrator derives the ledger from those two inputs.

That last part turned up a real bug on the orchestrator side. It read the stamped block straight onto the record, and an empty fairness_profile is documented as the claim 'won under unmodified rules'. So an adapter reporting only slot and difficulty - which is all an adapter can honestly know - would have made every AI-slot decision assert fair play on a game that had none, invisibly: nothing distinguishes 'no handicaps in force' from 'nobody filled the list in'. decide() now derives via fairness.profile when the inputs are present and the entries are not, and leaves an adapter that stamps its own entries alone for fairness.drift to check. Three tests.

Not yet verified against a running game - the JSON shape round-trips through the contract and the derived ledger is 12 handicaps at ai/transcend, but whether *DiffLevel and is_human read correctly mid-game belongs to na-b4v's live session.
